questions.q: Why query sys.dm_db_missing_index_details instead of trusting Lesson 5's plan reading alone?
options: A real diagnosis confirms a visual impression with actual DMV evidence rather than just an eyeballed plan
The execution plan from Lesson 5 was fabricated and can't be trusted
sys.dm_db_missing_index_details replaces the need to ever read a plan again
It is required by Azure SQL Database licensing before creating any index
questions.explain: The plan reading was a strong lead, but confirming it with the missing-index DMV turns an impression into real evidence.

questions.q: What does equality_columns list for this query?
options: PatientID — the exact column filtered on with = , which should lead the new index
Every column in the entire dbo.Invoices table
Only columns used in ORDER BY
The name of the existing clustered index
questions.explain: equality_columns lists PatientID, the column filtered with =, which is exactly what should lead the new nonclustered index.

questions.q: What are included_columns for, in Lesson 7's fix?
options: Candidates for INCLUDE — columns the query reads but doesn't filter on
Columns that must become the new clustering key
Columns that should be deleted from the table
Columns already covered by the existing clustered index
questions.explain: included_columns (InvoiceDate, Amount, Status, ProviderID) are read by the query but not filtered on — exactly what INCLUDE is for.

questions.q: Why doesn't the existing clustered index on InvoiceID help this query?
options: PatientID isn't the clustering key and no nonclustered index on PatientID exists, so every row must be checked
The clustered index was dropped accidentally last week
InvoiceID and PatientID are actually the same column
Clustered indexes never help any query in Azure SQL Database
questions.explain: The clustered index on InvoiceID is efficient for single-invoice lookups but useless for finding all invoices for a given patient.

questions.q: Why does Lesson 7 still re-capture a real execution plan after creating the index, instead of trusting avg_user_impact alone?
options: avg_user_impact is the optimizer's own estimate, not a measured fact, so the fix needs to be verified
avg_user_impact is always exactly accurate and verification is just a formality
Execution plans can only be captured once per database
CREATE INDEX statements never actually take effect in Azure SQL Database
questions.explain: Treating the optimizer's estimate as a hint rather than a guarantee, and verifying with a real plan afterward, is what separates a real fix from a guess.
